name: AJSIEM Alert Catalog
description: Stratified SIEM alerts for Kali → Graylog lab traffic (low / medium / high).

alerts.title: [LOW] Successful SSH authentication
alerts.description: Normal remote access. Track for baseline and account hygiene.
alerts.response: Verify expected users and source IPs; no immediate containment.

alerts.title: [LOW] Privileged command via sudo
alerts.description: Authorized elevation for routine admin work.
alerts.query: sudo AND COMMAND= AND NOT "incorrect password"
alerts.response: Spot-check COMMAND field against change windows.

alerts.title: [MEDIUM] Repeated SSH authentication failures
alerts.description: Possible password spraying or brute force against Kali/SSH.
alerts.response: Correlate source IPs; consider fail2ban / firewall block; reset targeted accounts.

alerts.title: [MEDIUM] New local user created
alerts.description: Account creation outside change control is suspicious on a lab attacker host.
alerts.response: Validate who created the account and whether it was authorized.

alerts.title: [HIGH] Direct root SSH login
alerts.description: Root interactive login is a critical control failure in most environments.
alerts.response: Isolate host if unexpected; rotate credentials; review auth logs and sessions.

alerts.title: [HIGH] Network scan / reconnaissance indicators
alerts.description: Nmap or SYN-flood style messages indicating active recon or DoS probing.
alerts.response: Identify scanner source; block at perimeter; capture PCAP if investigating.

alerts.title: [HIGH] Privilege escalation failure storm
alerts.description: Repeated failed sudo password attempts often precede or accompany compromise.
alerts.response: Lock account; inspect processes; check for persistence.
